reviews.author: Joon Smith
reviews.text:
I visited the Insa-dong art shop while looking for a place to relax after finishing work. As befits its name, it was a store that displayed and sold a variety of cars, and it seemed like it also had a separate display inside.
The exterior and interior of a hanok suitable for Insa-dong were nice to feel the traditional Korean style. We ordered milk tea drinking water and yakgwa.
The sweetness was subtle and blended well with the taste of the ingredients, making it delicious. The matcha grilled rice cake served as a service was light and delicious.

I had a great time thanks to the friendly service of the staff. This is a store you'll want to visit again the next time you stop by Insa-dong.

reviews.author: pathfinder
reviews.text: This is an herbal medicine-style cafe that I definitely want to take my foreign friends who are visiting Korea for the first time to. Of course, I think you will enjoy taking the elderly with you. If you order Ssanghwa tea, ginger tea, or any other herbal tea-related menu, they come with herbal medicine, honey, ginseng sprout pizza, and something that seems like they would be served at an herbal medicine store, along with the tea, as a side dish. The man gives something like a pill, and the woman gives something like a pill, but it tastes okay. The price is cheap compared to the various things that come with it (I think the drinks are cheap because they are heated and poured directly from the pack), so if you want to experience a unique cafe, it would be a good idea to visit. It really seems like it would be hard to find it anywhere other than Jongno...

After the plastic surgery group and Lee Blan group broke up,

The blanket group bought winter blankets at Gwangjang Market and headed to a spicy chicken stew restaurant recommended by a local. Although I ate raw beef and octopus for breakfast, it was difficult to refuse Jiaming's enthusiastic invitation.

When I arrived, the restaurant wasn't open yet, so I bought an Americano at a take-out coffee shop near the entrance and sat in the only seat inside. The coffee shop was small, and there was only one person making coffee and paying the bills. It had a very professional feel, with coffee beans and other ingredients piled high.

It was really nice to have a warm cup of coffee in the chilly weather. However, the coffee was a bit weak for my taste. The taste was okay, but I wouldn't say it was particularly great. The manager (I guess) was very patient in taking my order and made the coffee with great care.

reviews.author: Catherine Chen
reviews.text:
April 2, 2024. I bought coffee at a popular cafe near the hotel frequented by office workers! The coffee was really cheap! 😍

The coffee was really cheap and delicious! The taiyaki was also really delicious 🤤 The sweet red bean paste was a perfect match with Americano ❤️

The Americano cup looks big, but I think the coffee is a bit weak. I understand why Koreans drink coffee like water. If you are an office worker who drinks coffee often, I think three cups a day is enough 👌

The morning I bought it, many office workers were already ordering in advance, so it was very convenient to take out 👏 This cafe is really popular!

- I looked it up on the Internet and it turned out to be a chain takeout coffee shop! This is my favorite takeout coffee shop in Korea right now! It's cheap, delicious and convenient, so I highly recommend it to everyone 🥰

- But to be honest, it's rare to find cafes in Seoul that give discounts if you use eco-friendly cups. The transparent cups are pretty, but Seoul still seems to have room for improvement in terms of environmental protection.

Every Monday at 7 o'clock, various Korean antiques are auctioned (if you go before then, you can see a preview), and at other times, the highest grade teas are auctioned or various types of lectures are held.

It's one of the few great places left in Insadong. A love of Korean ceramics and tea

Every Monday at 7pm, a variety of Korean antiques are auctioned off (if you go before then, you can see a preview).
At other times, high-end teas are served or various classes are held.
Of course, you can also view or purchase the collection if you visit during business hours.

One of the few great places left in Insadong.
If you like Korean ceramics or tea, be sure to visit.

Every Monday at 7 p.m., the venue holds an auction featuring a variety of Korean antiques (and you can view the preview if you arrive beforehand).
At other times, they serve top-grade tea or host a range of lectures.
Of course, if you visit during business hours, you can also browse or purchase items from their collection.

It’s one of the few remarkable places remaining in Insadong. If you enjoy Korean ceramics or tea, you should definitely stop by.

reviews.author: Jessika Cantu
reviews.text:
I had no idea there was real fruit in the tea, but wow, it really exceeded my expectations! I tried the Apple Citron Hot Tea and the Grapefruit Hot Tea, and both were on a completely different level. The apple citron had real citrus slices floating around instead of artificial syrup flavor. The sweetness of the apple was perfectly balanced with the refreshing and tangy taste.

Grapefruit tea? There were fresh grapefruit slices in the cup. It had a slightly bitter taste typical of traditional grapefruit (which I like), but it became smoother when I added a little honey. I could feel the care put into the ingredients. There is absolutely no shortcut.

The warm, rich flavor of tea was just what I needed when walking around sightseeing in cold weather. I felt really at ease, especially when I was walking down the street. It's a shame I didn't have coffee this time, but I definitely want to come back and try it again.

Mega Coffee, definitely worth a visit again!

reviews.text: This is a place where you can eat vegan traditional tea, traditional Korean snacks, shaved ice, gelato, and more! There is also a vegan restaurant near Osegae Hyang, so it’s perfect for dessert! Haha, the shaved ice is for one person, so I think it would be good to order according to the number of people. reviews.author: Hyunwook Park
reviews.text: It is located on Ssamzie-gil in Insa-dong. The streets of Insa-dong itself are narrow and complicated, so it is difficult to find if you just go there, so I think you should use the directions to get there. It is located on one side of a narrow street, and as soon as you enter, there are traces and smells of the past that make you think, “Oh, this is Insa-dong.” It smelled like herbal medicine, which you cannot smell in coffee houses these days. There was a room and a table with chairs. The menu had sikhye crystal and Ssanghwa tea and Schisandra chinensis tea. There were a lot of different menu items from coffee shops these days, such as citron tea. I tried to order red bean shaved ice, but I couldn't because it was a limited menu in May. If you order tea as standard, rice cakes and Korean snacks were served as per person. I ordered misutgaru, and it was rich, savory, sweet, and delicious. Time passed quickly as I drank tea while looking at the many writings left on the wall and the old-fashioned props. This place had a similar feel everywhere but felt fresh. It was a good place

The softness of the coffee flavor was so refreshing that I keep thinking about it. In addition, the dessert had a meju-like feel and the stylish design matched the interior. It seems like I had a really good time with great feelings and emotions.

The 2nd floor has a loft feel and the 3rd floor has a rooftop, so no matter where you spend your time, it will leave you with memorable memories. Please note that the seats on the second floor are a bit uncomfortable.
The 3rd floor rooftop is outdoors and you can see Jongmyo Shrine, so it would be attractive in spring weather.

Meju-shaped cake dessert is a familiar taste, but the combination of cheese and toppings and the design surrounding it still remain in my memory.

reviews.author: BONG
reviews.text:
It is a cafe located in the middle of Seosunla-gil. It is a two-story tile-roofed house, but only the first floor is operated as a cafe.

Coffee Bay is not very well known, but some of the stores are located in pretty good locations.

When the weather is nice, there are quite a few tables on the sidewalk, and there are also some floor seats that are more like sit-down seats rather than outdoor seating. The direction from which the sun shines is attractive, and the direction facing away from the sun is also cluttered, but it is still quite nice to sit comfortably.

The interior is cluttered with tables very close together, and the lines for ordering and picking up food are very complicated. There seems to be only one employee even during the afternoon rush hour, and the downside is that it takes quite a long time even after ordering.

If the weather is good, the place is almost full and you have to time your order well.

The taste of the coffee is just mediocre, it's better to have juice or a special menu, and the bakery doesn't actually have any great merit, but it seems like it's good for cheap eating in moderation.

The location is attractive enough, and the outdoor seating is a big plus.

Last time I went to this store after eating soybean paste at Songnimwon, there were quite a few customers outside the store, so I looked and saw that it was a coffee shop and it wasn't registered on Manpl, so I registered it and stopped by today.

After parking in the alley near the store for a while, I headed toward the store while looking at Naver Map. It seemed like there were customers in front of the store, so I approached and found that it was not the Mirror Ball Coffee Stand, but a different coffee shop called Wonnam Gabae. After doing a quick search, it seemed to be a fairly famous coffee shop, so I decided to stop by next time and today, I looked at the Naver Map to find the Mirror Ball Coffee Stand that I had originally planned to stop by.

I don't really remember when I passed by and saw it, but it had a more simple exterior than I expected, so it didn't catch my eye at first, so I wandered around for a while, looking at the location on Naver Maps, and looking closely again, the retro-looking store caught my eye.

The store's glass door is a 180-degree revolving door, which is rare to see every now and then, so it feels somewhat new. I may have seen the store in passing before, but anyway, it feels a bit smaller than I remembered. There were two people in the store, and when I asked them what menu they were famous for, they asked me which one I liked, and I told them that I like coffee with a good acidity. There was only one type of coffee bean, so I couldn't choose, and they said something like a latte or an Einschpenner, so I originally ordered an iced Americano. I would have asked for it, but this time I would like an iced latte.

After handing over the card and looking at the menu again, I saw that the Americano was 2,000 won, the latte was 2,500 won, and the Einspänner was 4,000 won. Perhaps because it was literally a coffee stand and only takeout was possible, I thought to myself that this is my type of shop as long as the price is cheap and the taste is good.

It was prepared quickly and came out in a size that looked like a Starbucks Grande. When I took it out and got in the car and tasted it, I realized that it didn't have the acidity that I like, but that it had a moderate savory taste that is popular in Korea. Even though it doesn't have acidity, it has a unique savory taste and the price is cheap, so it's delicious...

It was a visit that made me want to visit again and also stop by Wonnam Gabae, which seemed to be a more famous store nearby.

reviews.author: Daniel Schweri
reviews.text: I visited at 10:30 and enjoyed delicious food, coffee, and friendly service. So I went again the next day at 9:30. Unfortunately, they said the food would start at 10pm, but I was willing to wait. Three tables were empty so I put my bag and jacket there. But the waiter told me that my table was reserved for another customer (even though all three tables were empty and there were no customers waiting). I had no choice but to pack my bags and leave them at the bar. Then I tried to pay for the coffee, but they didn't take cash. In conclusion, it is best to go between 10 and 11 o'clock when the food is served, and prepare to pay by credit card. And please keep in mind that even if the table is empty, there may be no seats available.
